verdict.rationale: GitBook documents its own CLI for working from the shell (listing organizations, inspecting spaces and pages, building and publishing integrations) and a RESTful API, so headless, scriptable operation is first-party. However, nothing in the pack describes CI pipeline usage, non-interactive auth, or automation recipes. A 2020 community note says the legacy open-source CLI is no longer actively developed, which lowers confidence but does not concretely contradict the current CLI. Missing for 10: explicit CI/pipeline integration docs (e.g. GitHub Actions usage, token-based non-interactive auth), evidence of the CLI's full command scope for automation, independent hands-on corroboration of headless/CI runs.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can run the product headlessly / in CI for automation
